title: Index Construction at Scale: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Index Construction at Scale: Visual Guide

1. Where Postings Come From | the bridge from lessons 01-03 (dictionary, postings, intersection, skip pointers) to building that index, with a block-capacity M slider over a corpus emitting T = 1 billion occurrences | blocked construction buys a hard memory bound almost for free because sort work is O(T log M) and the logarithm is over the block, not the corpus, so you pay in runs to merge and temporary storage

2. Build Runs, Merge Runs | a steppable three-way merge of runs A, B and C emitting cloud [1,4,8], database [5], search [7] and vector [2,3,6,9], plus a local-aggregation toggle | equal terms meet in the merge and their already-sorted postings join in one sequential pass over immutable files, while local aggregation collapses five occurrences in a document to one posting with five positions

3. The Binary Counter | logarithmic merge with B = 1,000: add batches and watch level 0 carry into 2B and 4B segments, with segment count, doc-writes and write amplification | at most one segment per level gives O(log N) segments and O(log N) write amplification instead of rebuilding the corpus per batch, and every live segment is searched on every query

4. Segments And Tombstones | a merge-policy slider from 12 lazy segments to 1, plus one query over four generations with generation-ordering switched on and off | merging trades write I/O for query fan-out, and without version semantics a superseded document returns twice and a tombstoned document comes back as a live result

5. Rebuild Or Merge | sliders for corpus size S, daily changed docs and write amplification W comparing W*delta against S, with two worked presets and four rebuild triggers | incremental wins when the delta is tiny relative to the corpus and rebuild wins when the corpus is small, but an analyzer or schema change, a 40% deletion wave or unexplained count drift overrides the arithmetic entirely
